key_insight: Low-dimensional perovskite capping increases surface roughness while preserving electronic uniformity, demonstrating that morphology and optoelectronic quality can be decoupled.
engineering_relevance: Capping layers offer a route to more durable perovskite photovoltaics and show why surface smoothness alone is an insufficient quality metric.
method: Cap 3D perovskites with Ruddlesden–Popper layers derived from 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium.
Combine statistical AFM with confocal spatially resolved photoluminescence and quasi-Fermi level splitting analysis.
Compare pristine and capped films before and after accelerated aging.
evidence_signal: Despite greater roughness and height asymmetry, capped films showed enhanced photoluminescence, reduced non-radiative recombination, and more uniform radiative quasi-Fermi level splitting, largely retaining optoelectronic homogeneity during aging.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative effect sizes, aging conditions, or device-level efficiency results, limiting assessment of practical performance gains.
paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
